evidence.text: We commenced operations in 1993 and have been profitable every year since inception. For fiscal years 2015 , 2014 and 2013 , our net sales were $1,991.2 million , $1,467.2 million and $1,162.6 million , respectively, and our net income was $101.9 million , $54.2 million and $21.3 million , respectively. Our increase in net income in fiscal year 2015 was primarily attributable to an increase in our gross profit resulting primarily from higher sales and improved gross margin and operating margin, partially offset by higher income tax expenses attributable to higher operating income.

attrs.numbers_show: Operating cash flow deteriorated by $51.1M. Working capital absorbed cash: receivables increased $109.9M (E7, E19), inventory increased $147.7M (E39), while current liabilities rose $143.2M (E11, E23). attrs.reason: Management provides no explicit explanation for the swing in operating cash flow (E33). While the defender reconciles the swing with working capital changes (receivables +$109.9M, inventory +$147.7M, current liabilities +$143.2M), this reconciliation is not from management's own statements and the MD&A does not address the CFO divergence.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The swing to negative operating cash flow is explained by deliberate working capital investment to support 35.7% revenue growth: inventory was built to meet anticipated FY2016 demand, receivables expanded with sales to distributors and OEMs, and the increase in current liabilities only partially offset these outflows.

attrs.final_verdict: explanation does not fit the numbers
